item.title: Three risks for Nvidia shares after Huang admits affair with suspected Chinese spy
item.description:
Monday’s US session is the first chance for Nvidia shares to trade on the admission and the board inquiry, and the short-term risk leans lower. Three pressure points stand out. The first is key-person and governance risk at a founder-led company while an investigation is open. The second is Washington scrutiny that could cloud Huang’s role in shaping chip policy. The third is the China export question, if officials decide his influence on access to Beijing has been compromised. Nvidia’s heavy index weighting means a sharp move would weigh on the Nasdaq, the S&P 500 and AI-linked chip names. Offsetting that, leadership is unchanged and nothing so far touches demand, supply or earnings, so the selling could fade unless the story escalates.

---

Huang’s admission turns a disputed intelligence story into a confirmed personal one. That leaves Nvidia’s board, Congress and investors weighing whether the fallout stays reputational or starts to touch leadership and China policy.

Summary:

  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted being unfaithful to his wife, apologising to his family and staff and taking full responsibility.
  • The relationship was with Alice Huang (Huang Le), a senior executive at Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom US officials reportedly believe was recruited by Chinese intelligence.
  • Nvidia’s board has opened an independent investigation led by independent directors and outside counsel, and says it has no reason to believe secrets or national security were compromised.
  • Huang remains CEO and will cooperate. Nvidia had earlier described the contacts as routine customer dealings.
  • House committee chairs have requested a briefing, while Beijing calls the spying claims groundless.
  • Nvidia shares fell around 3% after the first report in late October. Monday’s session is the first test since the admission.

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has admitted to an extramarital relationship with a business executive whom US officials reportedly believe was working for Chinese intelligence. It sets up a test for shares of the world’s most valuable company when US trading resumes on Monday.

In a draft email to staff obtained by Axios, Huang apologised to his family and to employees, writing “I was unfaithful to my wife.” He said he took full responsibility for falling short of his duties to the company, its board and its shareholders.

The woman at the centre of the story is Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company and Nvidia customer. She is not related to the Nvidia chief. Earlier reporting, citing US officials, said American intelligence had identified her as an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. According to those reports, she was tasked with gathering information from Huang and pushing for wider Chinese access to Nvidia’s advanced chips. Beijing has rejected the allegations as groundless, and none of the reporting has shown that Huang knowingly passed on sensitive information.

Nvidia’s board responded on Sunday by opening an independent investigation, overseen by a committee of independent directors with outside counsel. The board said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised, but that the inquiry would examine all available information. Huang will remain chief executive and has agreed to cooperate.

The admission marks a sharp shift from the company’s earlier stance. Since the first report surfaced in late October, Nvidia had described the contacts as routine dealings with a regional customer, noting that its chief executive meets thousands of customer executives each year. The shares fell around 3% on the day after that first report.

Pressure is also building in Washington. Republican chairs of House committees covering China, foreign affairs and intelligence have asked Huang for a briefing on the relationship and on Nvidia’s safeguards against espionage. President Donald Trump, who has relied on Huang as an adviser on artificial intelligence, has left open whether that role will continue.

For investors, the near-term question is whether this stays a governance and headline story or develops into something that touches Nvidia’s leadership or its access to China. The next markers to watch are further reporting on what information, if any, changed hands, the findings of the board’s inquiry and any congressional briefing. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: WTI oil price outlook: After a 17.5% slide, can buyers reclaim $92.53?
item.description:
Oil recovered from a sharp selloff, but buyers have struggled to hold higher prices. My analysis finds a bearish picture over the next several sessions, while the immediate outlook is much less decisive. Here are the levels and developments that could change the outlook. Let's jump into my crude oil futures analysis on the daily chart:

WTI crude oil futures are attempting to stabilize after a roughly 17.5% decline from their late-October high, but the rebound has not yet overturned the recent bearish trend. December futures settled Friday, November 6, at $90.83 per barrel. The next meaningful test for buyers lies between $91 and $92.53.

The interesting part is not simply that oil has fallen and bounced. It is that selling pressure appears to be losing some of its effectiveness, but buyers have yet to demonstrate that they can sustain a recovery.

That distinction could become particularly important as traders assess the next developments in the US-Iran conflict and their implications for global oil supply.

Oil's rebound has a problem: Buyers cannot hold their gains

WTI crude futures fell from approximately $104.99 in late October to $86.65 on November 5, a decline of about 17.5%.

From there, buyers managed to push prices back to $92.53 during Friday's session. But the recovery lost momentum, with our final market observation at $90.37 at 4:55 p.m. Eastern on November 6. That observation is separate from the day's official settlement of $90.83.

There is a potentially encouraging development for oil bulls. Recent attempts to push prices lower have not always produced lasting declines. That suggests the earlier selling pressure may be becoming less effective.

However, the opposite is also true. Buying interest has not consistently translated into sustained advances.

A market can stop falling rapidly without immediately becoming bullish.

The difference between a bounce and a genuine recovery is whether buyers can establish and defend higher prices.

Two market scores, two different conclusions

Our assessment of WTI crude futures, based on market evidence through November 6, produces two distinct readings:

Bigger picture: -6 out of 10 (bearish)

Over the recent weeks and looking toward the next several sessions, the market remains clearly tilted toward sellers. The rebound has not repaired the damage caused by the preceding decline.

Short term: -1 out of 10 (nearly balanced)

For the next one or two trading sessions, the evidence is considerably less directional. Buyers and sellers have both shown an ability to interrupt the other's progress.

The scoring scale runs from -10, representing exceptionally strong bearish pressure, to +10, representing exceptionally strong bullish pressure, with zero indicating a balanced market. These scores are directional assessments, not probabilities or automatic trading signals.

Remeber, oil traders: A market can remain bearish overall while offering a meaningful short-term recovery. The challenge is determining whether that recovery is developing into something more substantial.

WTI crude oil: Three scenarios worth watching

The next sustained move around $90-$92.53 could provide important information about the direction of oil prices.

1. Bullish scenario: A recovery above $92.53 changes the picture

The first encouraging development would be a move above $91.00-$91.32, followed by evidence that prices can remain above this area.

That would indicate that the recovery is gaining some traction.

The more significant test comes at $92.53, Friday's session high.

A sustained break above that level, particularly if oil can successfully hold it on a subsequent pullback, would strengthen the argument that buyers are regaining control.

If this happens, the next historical price references to monitor are:

  • $93.59: The first higher area where the recovery could face another test.

  • $95.15: A further upside reference if buying continues.

These are potential reaction levels, not predictions that oil will necessarily reach them.

A failed recovery that sends prices back below $90 would weaken this bullish scenario.

2. Bearish scenario: Failure around $91 puts $89.07 back in focus

The bearish scenario becomes more convincing if oil cannot recover $91 and instead falls back below $90.00-$90.05, remaining beneath that area.

That would suggest buyers are still unable to maintain higher prices.

The next important level would be $89.07, Friday's trading-session low.

A sustained break beneath $89.07 would increase the possibility of another decline toward the lower historical support area at $87.13-$86.65.

This would reinforce the broader bearish assessment.

Conversely, recovering and holding above the broken levels would weaken the bearish interpretation.

3. Neutral scenario: Oil remains trapped around $90-$91

Not every market needs to produce an immediate directional opportunity.

WTI could continue moving back and forth around $90-$91 without establishing a sustained breakout.

That would be consistent with the nearly balanced short-term score.

In such conditions, isolated moves above resistance or below support can produce misleading signals. Waiting for evidence that prices can hold beyond an important level may provide a clearer picture than reacting to every price fluctuation.

Why geopolitics could overwhelm the technical picture

There is an important fundamental dimension to this oil price outlook.

Much of the recent volatility has been associated with shifting expectations about the US-Iran conflict and the prospects for restoring more reliable oil shipments from the Middle East.

As investingLive recently explained, the possibility of de-escalation has created downward pressure on oil prices, while renewed military action remains a risk.

Reports of tanker attacks have also revived concerns about regional supply disruptions.

This creates two quite different potential drivers of oil prices:

De-escalation and improved supply conditions: Reduced fears of disruption could remove some of the geopolitical risk premium embedded in oil prices, potentially reinforcing the recent decline.

Renewed conflict or shipping disruptions: An increase in perceived supply risks could support oil prices or produce another sharp recovery, even if the recent technical trend remains bearish.

There are also conventional supply-and-demand considerations.

On November 1, seven OPEC+ producers announced that they would maintain their required production levels for December at September's levels.

Meanwhile, the latest US Energy Information Administration inventory report, released November 4, showed US commercial crude inventories declining by approximately 0.9 million barrels in the week ending October 30.

The inventory decline is a reminder that a sharp oil selloff does not necessarily mean every indicator of physical supply and demand is weakening.

For the coming week, the next scheduled EIA petroleum inventory release is Thursday, November 12, at noon Eastern, delayed because of the Veterans Day holiday.

What falling oil prices might mean for stocks, inflation and currencies

Even investors who never trade crude oil directly may find the next move informative.

Oil prices influence several important parts of the global economy, but their meaning depends heavily on why prices are changing.

Consider two very different reasons for lower oil prices.

If oil declines because supply disruptions are easing, that could help reduce energy-related inflation pressure and eventually benefit fuel-intensive businesses.

But if oil declines because economic demand is deteriorating, the same price movement could signal a less encouraging outlook for economic activity and corporate earnings.

There is another distinction worth remembering: Lower crude prices do not automatically translate into equally large declines in gasoline or diesel prices.

Refining capacity, fuel inventories and the margins earned by refineries can influence what consumers and businesses actually pay. This is an important theme in investingLive's recent analysis of oil refining margins and the prospects for normalizing fuel prices.

For energy-company investors, lower crude prices may pressure producers' revenues and margins, while companies that consume significant amounts of fuel could benefit. The outcome also depends on each company's cost structure, hedging and broader economic conditions.

For currency traders, changes in oil prices can influence the economic outlook for oil-exporting and oil-importing countries, although exchange rates respond to many other forces as well.

Oil should therefore be treated as a supporting market signal, not a stand-alone forecast for inflation, stocks, bonds or currencies.

What would convince us that oil's outlook is changing?

For now, the evidence supports a relatively straightforward conclusion.

WTI's recent-weeks trend remains bearish, but there are signs that the preceding selloff is losing some of its force. The immediate outlook is more balanced, and neither buyers nor sellers have decisively established control.

A sustained recovery above $91.00-$91.32, followed by a convincing move above $92.53, would strengthen the case for higher oil prices.

Conversely, renewed weakness below $90, followed by a sustained break of $89.07, would increase the risk of another move toward $87.13-$86.65.

And if oil continues fluctuating between these areas, the most useful conclusion may simply be that the market has not yet made its next directional decision.

The analysis refers specifically to NYMEX December 2026 WTI crude futures, with market evidence through November 6, 2026. The levels are historical references, not live prices or guaranteed support and resistance. Other futures expiries and oil instruments may trade at different prices.

item.title: Gold analysis: Buyers keep defending $4,040. Is $4,140 the next target?

Gold futures buyers keep returning near $4,040. Is $4,140 the next test?

Gold's recovery looks more convincing than Friday's volatile price action suggests. Buyers have repeatedly defended an important support area, and underlying trading activity points to improving buying effectiveness. But one resistance zone still stands between gold and a potentially larger rebound.

Gold futures are showing signs that buyers may be gaining the upper hand after a volatile week. The recovery from Friday's low of $4,035.10 is encouraging, but my bullish interpretation goes beyond that single rebound. Several developments suggest that gold may be preparing for another attempt toward $4,135-$4,140, provided buyers can overcome nearby resistance.

Why I see more bullish signs than bearish ones in gold

One price area stands out in my analysis: $4,040-$4,050.

Around $4,040 sits the October 29 point of control (POC), the price at which the greatest amount of trading volume occurred during that session.

That makes it a useful reference for understanding where buyers and sellers previously conducted significant business.

Gold moved above this level on November 4, retested the area and subsequently continued its advance.

The rally eventually carried futures beyond $4,150 on November 5.

What happened next is particularly interesting.

The market retraced sharply, and on Friday, November 6, gold returned to approximately $4,035, briefly moving beneath that important $4,040 reference.

Once again, buyers responded.

Gold recovered toward $4,080, reclaiming both the $4,040 area and the psychologically important $4,050 level.

To me, the repeated response around this price region is a meaningful bullish development. It suggests buyers have been willing to defend an area that previously attracted considerable trading activity.

Of course, support can eventually fail. But until it does, repeated rebounds deserve attention.

What the underlying trading activity tells us

Our deeper examination of Friday's trading adds another dimension to this interpretation.

The initial recovery attempt was unsuccessful. Sellers returned, and the market struggled to establish upward momentum.

Later, however, conditions improved.

Selling pressure became less effective at producing additional downside progress. Buyers established a higher low and subsequently achieved a stronger recovery.

Trading activity also became concentrated at higher prices during the rebound, suggesting improving buyer participation.

This is the part of the analysis I find especially constructive.

It is one thing for gold to bounce because selling temporarily stops. It is another for buyers to begin achieving progressively better price results.

Friday's developments showed elements of the latter.

Nevertheless, this remains an early indication rather than proof that sellers have lost control. Gold still needs to demonstrate that it can sustain trading above nearby resistance.

Three technical reasons the recovery may have further to run

Beyond Friday's buying activity, the broader price structure provides additional support for the bullish argument.

1. The recovery developed from a substantial base

Gold reached $3,879.30 on October 30 before stabilizing over the following sessions.

From October 30 into the beginning of November 4, the market established a foundation for a potential reversal.

The subsequent advance toward $4,155.80 represented a recovery of more than $275 per ounce from that October low.

That is a meaningful move, not merely a minor intraday bounce.

The correction that followed has been substantial, but it has not erased the entire advance.

2. Multiple technical references converge near $4,040

In addition to October 29's point of control, an October 27 volume-weighted average price (VWAP) reference sits near $4,038.

VWAP measures the average trading price weighted by volume. Historical VWAP references can sometimes become important areas where the market reassesses previous trading activity.

The proximity of these references to Friday's $4,035.10 low creates an interesting support cluster.

That does not make the cluster unbreakable, but it provides a reason to pay close attention to how gold behaves when returning to this area.

3. Friday's recovery reclaimed another important reference

Friday's VWAP was approximately $4,069.

The latest chart snapshot shows gold finishing near $4,080, above that reference and above the $4,050 support region.

For me, that is another encouraging observation.

After a significant intraday decline, recovering above the session's volume-weighted average suggests that buyers were capable of regaining meaningful ground.

The market did not simply stop falling. It recovered into a more constructive position.

The bigger picture: Three timeframes are beginning to support the recovery

The daily chart shows an emerging reversal attempt following October's substantial correction.

The four-hour chart shows the first meaningful pullback following the advance toward $4,155.80.

The hourly chart, meanwhile, shows early stabilization and improving short-term momentum.

These developments can coexist without contradiction.

A daily bullish recovery can experience a four-hour correction while the hourly chart begins signaling renewed buying interest.

The important question is whether the shorter-term recovery can develop into another advance on the higher timeframes.

For now, the technical evidence is encouraging but not fully aligned.

What could take gold toward $4,135-$4,140?

Although my interpretation leans bullish, the market still faces an important obstacle.

The immediate resistance area is $4,084-$4,092.

Gold needs to establish sustained trading above this region to strengthen the case that buyers are taking control.

A convincing break would bring $4,098-$4,116 into focus.

Beyond that, I would be watching $4,123-$4,135 and particularly the $4,135-$4,140 resistance area, which I consider a plausible next destination for the recovery.

That would place gold within striking distance of its previous $4,155.80 recovery high.

My view is not that gold must travel to $4,140.

Rather, the repeated defense of lower prices, improving underlying buying activity and broader recovery structure make that an increasingly interesting possibility.

A failure to overcome $4,092 would delay this scenario and could lead to another test of support.

Bullish scenario: Above $4,092

Sustained trading above $4,092 would strengthen the recovery outlook.

  • First partial-profit target: $4,104

  • Third partial-profit target: $4,149

The $4,135-$4,140 resistance region remains an important area to assess between the second and third targets.

A successful retest of former resistance would provide more convincing evidence than a brief move above the threshold.

Bearish scenario: Below $4,050

  • First partial-profit target: $4,039

  • Second partial-profit target: $4,007

A further decline below Friday's $4,035.10 low would be more significant, raising the risk of a deeper correction.

Neutral scenario: Between $4,050 and $4,092

Gold remains within a decision area until either side demonstrates more convincing control.

Traders may prefer to monitor price behavior near the boundaries rather than chase a move in the middle.

My outlook for gold: Bullish, but confirmation still matters

Having examined the underlying trading activity alongside the broader technical structure, I currently see more encouraging bullish signs than bearish ones.

Perhaps most importantly, selling pressure appears to be losing some of its effectiveness.

That leads me to favor the possibility of another recovery attempt, potentially toward $4,135-$4,140.

If gold cannot overcome $4,092, my expectation needs to be reassessed. If the market subsequently loses $4,050 and breaks below $4,035, the immediate bullish argument becomes substantially weaker.

For now, the evidence suggests buyers are fighting back effectively. The next test is whether they can turn that improvement into sustained progress above resistance.

item.title: Equity close: Decent rebound or a dead-cat bounce
item.description:
US stock markets started strong and we saw 10% bounces in beaten-up memory stocks. It didn't last but it also didn't break down. 

Some notable names:

  • MU +5.1%
  • SNDK +3.5%
  • INTC +7.7%
  • SKHY +2.8%
  • NVDA +2.8%
  • QCOM +5.8%

The hyperscalers were near flat and the indexes were higher but didn't finish at the highs. I wouldn't give the win today to the bulls or the bears. It was a nice day but came after a brutal rout. Non-farm payrolls may have limited the enthusiasm because it puts a rate hiking cycle back on the table.

Weighing at one point was a report on a strategy shift from MSFT where they will curb third-party data centers, with Oracle cited. That briefly sent ORCL 3% lower and weighed on the Nasdaq. Overall, it was a tough week for stocks but the pain was concentrated heavily in just a few names.

On the day:

  • Nasdaq Comp +1.1%
  • Russell 2000 +1.0%
  • DJIA -0.4%

On the week:

That tells me there is some optimism priced in now and that the market needs to see something official.
